docs.title: Day 1: Audience and Sales Pitch Plan
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Audience and Message
  • Objective: Students will identify a sales or marketing career opportunity and use FYF pitch evidence to plan an accurate audience-specific hook, offer, benefit, and call to action.
  • TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Completed FYF 30 Seconds to Sell work plus a two-page individual audience/assumption check, ethical boundary, career/work-product connection, and selected oral route.

TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B) Evidence: FYF pitch plus individual audience, accuracy, career, transfer, and oral-route evidence

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Per student, have FYF pp. 241-243, a pencil, and one two-page companion by private Canvas annotation or print. Use one labeled tray or the private Canvas collector. Project this complete model: Audience: busy students. Fact: the fictional service offers 20-minute review sessions. Benefit: review can fit between activities. Safe action: compare the two session options. Boundary: do not claim the service guarantees a grade. Preassign Day 2 live, conference, recording, or AAC routes. H&L, a real product, a public pitch, and printing are not required.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Persuasion warm-up - 5 min. Identify a hook, reason/benefit, and request.
  2. Read SparkClean - 8 min. Label hook, offer, benefit, and call to action; flag any real-world claim that would need verification.
  3. Define offer and audience - 10 min. Use FYF Step 2-3 and distinguish audience evidence from assumption.
  4. Plan four parts - 12 min. Complete FYF Step 4 with concise, accurate language.
  5. Write the full pitch - 10 min. Complete FYF Step 5 and the companion evidence that the workbook does not collect.
  6. Exit - 5 min. Name one transferable skill and one sales/marketing career work product.

docs.title: Key and Trim Point
docs.text: At minute 13, students should be able to point to the hook, offer, benefit, and call to action. If one-third confuse a feature and benefit, contrast 20-minute session with fits between activities. At minute 30, require an audience situation and supplied fact or labeled reason. At minute 44, check the ethical boundary, career connection, and Day 2 route. Trim optional sharing first; preserve all four pitch parts and companion evidence. Collect one route and return workbooks.

docs.title: Absence and Access
docs.text: The locked FYF images plus the two-page companion are the complete no-workbook route. Students may type, dictate, annotate, enlarge, or use paper. The Day 2 route may be live, conference, recording, or AAC.

docs.title: Day 2: Deliver, Test, and Revise a Sales Pitch
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Oral Revision
  • Objective: Students will communicate an audience-specific pitch twice, use feedback to make one visible revision, and explain how the communication skill transfers to a second career.
  • TEKS: d(4)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Two timed oral/AAC pitch attempts, one specific feedback point, a visible before/after revision, and a two-career transfer response.

TEKS: d(4)(B) Evidence: two timed oral/AAC attempts, specific feedback, visible revision, and two-career transfer

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Per student, have the Day 1 pitch, a pencil, and one two-page delivery record by private Canvas annotation or print. One timer serves the class. Set live partner, small-group, teacher-conference, recorded audio/video, and AAC routes before class. Project this before-feedback-after model: Before: “Sign up now.” Feedback: the next step is vague. After: “Compare the two fictional session options and circle the one that fits your schedule.” Effect: the audience knows the safe next action. Recorded students upload the written record and private audio/video together. Live, conference, and AAC students submit the written record while the teacher records student, date, route, both attempt times, feedback/revision, and oral/AAC completion. Do not make partner attendance or camera use a requirement.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Delivery model - 5 min. Demonstrate understandable pace, organization, and a safe call to action.
  2. Silent accuracy check - 5 min. Students remove unsupported urgency, guarantees, health, popularity, or income claims.
  3. First delivery - 10 min. Record route, time, and evidence.
  4. Feedback - 8 min. Partner, teacher, self-recording, transcript, or checklist identifies one strength and one specific revision.
  5. Revise - 10 min. Preserve before/after language and reason.
  6. Second delivery - 7 min. Apply the revision and record time/effect.
  7. Exit - 5 min. Name transferable communication evidence and next goal.

docs.title: Key and Trim Point
docs.text: At minute 15, check Attempt 1 time and one exact strength. If one-third give trait feedback, return to the before-feedback-after model. At minute 31, require visible before/after language and a reason tied to audience need. At minute 44, check Attempt 2 time, effect, and transfer. Do not score accent, eye contact, camera use, confidence, or memorization. Trim class share-outs first; preserve the second attempt and visible revision. Collect one record.

docs.title: Absence and Access
docs.text: Students may complete a teacher conference, private recording, or AAC attempt later. A written draft alone is not mislabeled oral evidence unless an accommodation changes the task.

docs.title: Day 3: BrainBoost Rescue and Career Oral Outline
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Problem Solving
  • Objective: Students will identify how a sales, marketing, or design career uses evidence to define a campaign problem, screen solutions, and organize a bounded career brief.
  • TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Completed FYF BrainBoost work plus a two-page individual cause statement, evidence-linked decision, fixed-source career outline, and cross-career problem-solving connection.

TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B) Evidence: FYF BrainBoost work plus individual cause/evidence, career outline, and transfer evidence

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Per student, have FYF pp. 244-247, a pencil, and one two-page companion by private Canvas annotation or print. Project both supplied models. Cause/evidence: “Result: sales are low. Evidence: students say the snack looks like other snacks and the reason to try it is unclear. Possible cause: the campaign does not communicate a distinct value.” Career outline: “Market research analysts study consumer preferences. A bachelor's degree is typical. BLS reports a $76,950 May 2024 U.S. median and 7% projected growth for 2024-34. Those measures are not DFW starting pay or a guarantee.” Sticky notes are optional. The three fixed career cards remove prior-research and login dependencies.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Problem-versus-result warm-up - 5 min. Low sales are a result; unclear value is a possible cause supported by supplied feedback.
  2. Analyze evidence - 8 min. Review FYF pp. 244-245: message, visuals, audience, and three customer comments.
  3. Generate/screen solutions - 10 min. Use FYF p. 246; reject invented health, nutrition, discount, scarcity, popularity, or data claims.
  4. Build the rescue - 10 min. Complete FYF p. 247 and record the individual cause/evidence decision in the companion.
  5. Select career evidence - 7 min. Prior verified evidence or fixed BLS fallback; keep measure/date/geography visible.
  6. Outline oral brief - 7 min. Opening, duty, preparation, labor evidence, bounded conclusion.
  7. Exit - 3 min. Name one transfer from campaign problem solving to the selected career.

docs.title: Key and Trim Point
docs.text: At minute 13, students should distinguish the low-sales result from a message/value cause. If one-third blame the audience, reread the supplied reach fact and comments. At minute 31, require the selected solution to answer exact evidence without adding a claim. At minute 44, require duty, preparation, measure, geography/date, and limitation in one outline. BrainBoost reached its stated audience; the issue is weak differentiation/need/message. Trim campaign-sketch polish first and provide the fixed career card; preserve cause/evidence, rejected claim, transfer, and outline. Collect the companion.

docs.title: Absence and Access
docs.text: The locked FYF images plus the two-page companion are the complete no-workbook route. Students may work independently; no partner, H&L, prior portfolio, or open-web search is required.

docs.title: Day 4: Interview Appearance and Career-Brief Rehearsal
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Interview Appearance
  • Objective: Students will describe context-appropriate interview appearance across office, task-demonstration, and virtual settings, then rehearse a career brief twice using an appropriate private recording, Canvas evidence card, teacher-approved visual, or AAC technology route.
  • TEKS: d(6)(B), d(4)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Three context decisions with verification questions, retryable practice Quiz feedback, two timed oral/AAC career rehearsals using one appropriate technology choice, and one visible revision.

TEKS: d(6)(B), d(4)(C) Evidence: three context decisions, retryable practice Quiz, and two rehearsals

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Per student, have one two-page landscape companion, a pencil, the private rehearsal-record Assignment, linked practice Quiz access, and the Day 3 outline. One timer serves the class. Students complete one record route by Canvas annotation/upload/text or paper; do not assign both. Preassign live, conference, private-recording, or AAC routes. Every route names appropriate technology: timer plus evidence card/teacher-approved visual, private recording, or AAC device. Project this rehearsal model: Attempt 1 omitted the labor-evidence limit. Revision: add “This U.S. median does not guarantee my pay.” Attempt 2 includes the limit while the evidence card keeps the source label visible. Do not require clothing modeling or personal cost/body/culture/religion/disability disclosure.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Context-first warm-up - 5 min. Appropriate appearance depends on workplace, task, safety, format, and accommodation.
  2. Three scenarios - 12 min. Office/customer-facing, skilled-trade task demonstration, and virtual interview.
  3. Practice Quiz - 8 min. Check source labels, appearance context, PPE confirmation, virtual readiness, and oral-route equivalence.
  4. Rehearsal 1 - 8 min. 60-90 seconds; capture content/delivery evidence.
  5. Feedback and revision - 7 min. Teacher, peer, self-recording, transcript, or checklist.
  6. Rehearsal 2 - 7 min. Apply revision.
  7. Exit - 3 min. One content check and one delivery/AAC check.

docs.title: Key and Trim Point
docs.text: Use these context models: office/customer-facing = clean functional clothing plus workplace/access verification; task demonstration = clean work clothing plus exact site PPE/tool verification; virtual = tested audio, private background, notifications off, backup route, and verified access expectations. At minute 17, each scenario needs a functional choice and question. If one-third write fashion rules, return to workplace/task/safety/format/accommodation. At minute 33, check Attempt 1 oral/AAC evidence and named technology. At minute 45, require Attempt 2 and a visible revision. Trim the Quiz to catch-up and remove class modeling first; preserve both rehearsals and technology evidence. Submit the Canvas record or collect one labeled paper companion, then close devices.

docs.title: Absence and Access
docs.text: Students may use teacher conference, private recording, or AAC. Virtual fallback includes audio/phone/approved reschedule planning when video or bandwidth fails.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Career Oral Evidence
  • Objective: Students will deliver a 60-90-second oral/AAC career brief using an appropriate private recording, Canvas evidence card, teacher-approved visual, or AAC technology route, with one duty, preparation evidence, a correctly labeled labor figure, and a bounded conclusion.
  • TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B), d(4)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Private 60-90-second oral/AAC career brief with one appropriate technology choice, two-page delivery record, two-career transfer reflection, 16-point self-score, and one visible revision note.

TEKS: d(1)(C), d(4)(B), d(4)(C) Evidence: 60-90-second professional oral/AAC brief, self-evidence, transfer reflection, and rubric

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Per student, have the two-page Career Oral Evidence Brief, two-page rubric, Day 3 outline, and assigned technology. Prepare one class roster/checkoff and timer. Checkoff fields are student, career, date, route, seconds, technology used, oral/AAC complete, written record complete. Confirm each route before class. Use sequential 60-90-second slots, simultaneous small groups with recordable evidence, teacher conferences, private recordings, or AAC. Project this complete model: “I am exploring market research analysis because the work studies what audiences need. Analysts collect and explain consumer evidence; a bachelor's degree is typical. BLS reports a $76,950 May 2024 U.S. median and 7% projected growth for 2024-34. Those measures do not guarantee DFW starting pay. My next step is to compare the work with graphic design.” Do not improvise a 75-minute three-minute roster.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Final evidence check - 5 min. Career, duty, preparation, labeled labor evidence, bounded conclusion, source, and time.
  2. Oral/AAC evidence window - 35 min. Use the preassigned route; students not presenting complete private self-evidence and transfer reflection.
  3. Self-score and revision note - 7 min. Use four criteria; identify one next change.
  4. Week 5 interview preview - 3 min. This is not graded today. The next week uses a private campus route and does not collect family contact information.

docs.title: Key and Trim Point
docs.text: At minute 5, every student needs a route, slot, and named technology. If one-third are not ready, use the complete fixed model and conference queue. At minute 25, the checkoff should show at least half of oral/AAC routes complete while waiting students finish written evidence. At minute 43, every student needs oral/AAC completion plus the written record/self-score or a named make-up slot. Recorded students upload the written record/rubric and private audio/video together. Live, conference, and AAC students submit the written record/rubric by annotation, upload, labeled text, or paper while the teacher completes the named checkoff. Text alone is not oral evidence. Trim public sharing and the Week 5 preview first; preserve oral/AAC evidence, appropriate technology, written record, and checkoff.

docs.title: Absence and Access
docs.text: Use a supervised teacher conference, private recording, or AAC make-up. No public Discussion or family-adult dependency.

docs.title: Week 4: Sales and Career Oral Evidence
docs.text: 6th Six Weeks · 5 class periods (50 minutes each)

docs.title: Learning Target
docs.text: I can identify sales/marketing careers, plan and revise an ethical audience-specific pitch, transfer problem-solving and communication skills across careers, describe context-appropriate interview appearance, and deliver a concise professional oral career brief.

docs.title: Turnkey Week Structure
docs.text: Day Focus Required evidence Canvas interaction 1 audience + pitch anatomy FYF pitch plus individual audience/accuracy/career evidence private annotation Assignment 2 oral pitch + revision two communicated attempts, visible revision, and transfer record private upload/annotation Assignment + teacher oral/AAC checkoff 3 BrainBoost rescue + career evidence FYF campaign work plus individual decision and 60-90-second career outline private annotation Assignment 4 interview appearance + rehearsal three context decisions and two rehearsals private rehearsal-record Assignment + linked retryable practice Quiz 5 career oral evidence 60-90-second live/recorded/AAC brief, reflection, and self-score private two-part formative Assignment + teacher oral/AAC checkoff

docs.title: TEKS
docs.text:
• d(1)(C): identify sales, marketing, and selected career opportunities/work products (Days 1, 3, 5).
  • d(4)(B): identify transferable problem-solving, audience, organization, and communication skills (Days 1-5).
  • d(4)(C): give an oral professional presentation on career/college exploration using appropriate technology (Days 4-5; Day 5 primary evidence). Day 2 is product-pitch practice and does not claim this standard.
  • d(6)(B): describe appropriate appearance for an interview using workplace, task, safety, virtual-format, and accommodation context (Day 4).

docs.title: Evidence and Access Boundaries
docs.text:
• The final brief lasts 60-90 seconds and may be live whole group, live small group, teacher conference, recorded audio/video, or AAC/speech-generating device. Every route uses appropriate evidence or assistive technology. A written outline supports oral evidence but does not replace it unless an accommodation formally changes the task.
  • Recorded students upload the written record/rubric and private audio/video together. Live, conference, and AAC students submit the written record/rubric while the teacher records student, career, date, route, seconds, technology, oral/AAC completion, and written completion on the class checkoff.
  • No student is required to present for three minutes to a full class. The schedule is planned before Day 1 rather than improvised on presentation day.
  • Required content uses verified prior research or one of three fixed BLS fallback cards. Dated U.S. medians are never relabeled DFW starting pay.
  • Pitch and BrainBoost work are fictional. Students do not sell, post, link, collect data, make health/income/popularity/scarcity claims, or use real contact/payment information.
  • Interview appearance is context-first and access-neutral. Brand, cost, body, culture, religion, disability, gender expression, camera use, accent, and public-speaking confidence are not scored.
  • H&L is optional. No Xello or eDynamic completion task belongs here.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
• Canvas paired guides, five compact companion/evidence tools, and one formative rubric
  • locked compressed FYF pp. 241-247, 280, and 299
  • Chromebook/microphone or live/AAC route; paper; visible timer
  • current CareerOneStop interview guidance, BLS occupation pages, and Irving ISD CTE pages

docs.title: Grading
docs.text: Days 1-5 are formative rehearsal for the Week 5 interview and Week 6 capstone. The 6SW assessment map does not create a separate Week 4 grade. Use the 16-point rubric for feedback and revision. Clothing cost/style, platform, eye contact, accent, speech difference, camera use, English mechanics, and performance confidence are not scored unless meaning is unclear.

docs.title: Current Sources
docs.text:
• CareerOneStop: Get Ready to Interview
  • CareerOneStop: Dress for Success
  • BLS Sales Managers
  • BLS Market Research Analysts
  • BLS Graphic Designers
  • Irving ISD High School CTE

docs.title: Day 1: Job Search and Posting Screen
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Job Search
  • Objective: Students will identify and apply the steps of an effective job search by sequencing a safe search cycle, screening a fictional posting, and selecting an authorized next action.
  • TEKS: d(6)(A)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Two-page job-search and posting-screen decision record.

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Post the Student Annotation and the two-page record. Default printing is zero. Display the seven-step strip and confirm that the Pecan Creek posting is fictional, not a vacancy.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Bellringer - 5 min. Put seven job-search actions in a first-draft order. Students mark one step they are unsure about.
  2. Model the cycle - 8 min. Target, prepare, search, screen, track, tailor/apply, follow up. Emphasize that screening occurs before personal data or contact.
  3. Notice and label - 10 min. Read the fixed posting. Mark job duties, qualifications, evidence limits, and facts that would require verification in a real search.
  4. Posting screen - 17 min. Students identify two truthful matches, one honest gap, two verification checks, and the authorized next action.
  5. Turn and talk - 5 min. Partners compare one match and one risk. Students revise their own record.
  6. Exit - 5 min. Name the search step most likely to be skipped and the consequence.

docs.title: Monitor, Key, and Trim Point
docs.text: Full evidence puts the seven actions in a defensible order, distinguishes a posting from independent employer verification, uses two supplied matches, keeps one gap visible, and chooses a safe next action. A job-board result is a lead, not proof. Trim the optional partner share before reducing the individual screen.

docs.title: Supports and Access
docs.text: Keep posting/oferta de empleo, screen/revisar, verify/verificar, evidence/evidencia, and authorized/autorizado visible beside the posting screen. Use the frame: “I would verify [detail] through [official or known route] before [action].” Students may type, annotate, dictate, use enlarged print, or use paper. A live job board, H&L, FYF Rung 5, employer contact, account, or personal data is not required.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Business Correspondence
  • Objective: Students will write appropriate business correspondence by tailoring a fictional cover letter to a posting, using supplied evidence, and making one visible revision.
  • TEKS: d(7)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Three-page fictional cover-letter plan, draft, evidence audit, and final revision.

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Post the private Assignment, three-page cover-letter packet, and two-page Major rubric. Keep the fictional posting and Jordan evidence card visible. The letter is not sent.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Bellringer - 5 min. Decide which three statements belong in a resume, cover letter, or neither.
  2. Model - 8 min. Show the four jobs of the letter: name the position, connect evidence, explain fit without invention, and close courteously.
  3. Plan - 9 min. Match two supplied Jordan facts to two posting needs and name one gap that must remain honest.
  4. Draft - 13 min. Write three short paragraphs. Students may use the complete sentence frames, then revise the wording into Jordan's plain voice.
  5. Audit and final - 10 min. Check every claim against the evidence card, remove generic or inflated language, and make one before/after revision visible.
  6. Exit - 5 min. Explain why the revision made the letter more accurate, specific, or useful.

docs.title: Monitor, Key, and Trim Point
docs.text: A strong simulation letter names the role, uses two accurate evidence links, stays concise, acknowledges no false credential or work history, and includes a courteous next step. Requirements vary: a real applicant follows the posting about whether a cover letter is required. Trim peer exchange before planning, final-writing, or revision time.

docs.title: Supports and Access
docs.text: Keep requirement/requisito, evidence/evidencia, tailor/adaptar, qualification/cualificación, and revision/revisión beside the plan. Use the frame: “Your posting asks for [need]. Jordan demonstrated [skill] when [action and result].” Accept typing, annotation, dictation, enlarged print, or paper. Score evidence and meaning, not formulaic enthusiasm or perfect English mechanics.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Applications and References
  • Objective: Students will complete a sample job application and explain protocol for selecting and using references by using supplied fictional information and asking permission before sharing.
  • TEKS: d(7)(C), d(7)(D)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Four-page fictional application, reference-role plan, unsent permission request, and privacy audit.

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Post the private Student Annotation and four-page packet. Students use Jordan Rivera from start to finish. Do not collect, display, or ask students to destroy real application or reference data.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Bellringer - 5 min. Sort four fields into “use supplied fact,” “use N/A,” or “do not provide in this simulation.”
  2. Application model - 7 min. Read directions first, use a specific target, complete applicable fields, keep evidence consistent, and use N/A only when a field does not apply.
  3. Chunked application - 18 min. Complete target and education, then experience, skills, and fictional availability. Pause after each section for an active-monitoring check.
  4. Reference protocol - 8 min. Select roles that observed the relevant work. Separate teacher, activity sponsor, and adult supervisor evidence.
  5. Permission draft and audit - 7 min. Draft but do not send the request. Ask before sharing any contact route.
  6. Exit - 5 min. Explain how permission protects the applicant, reference, and employer.

docs.title: Monitor, Key, and Trim Point
docs.text: Full evidence uses only supplied facts, completes applicable fields or N/A, matches the cover letter, selects reference roles with firsthand evidence, and asks permission before sharing. No student enters a real name, contact route, availability, ID, signature, health, family, or immigration information. Trim optional comparison before the consistency/privacy audit.

docs.title: Supports and Access
docs.text: Keep applicable/aplicable, N/A/no aplica, consistent/coherente, reference/referencia, and permission/permiso beside the form. Use the frame: “I chose the [role] because that person observed Jordan [action].” Short fields receive short spaces; evidence and rationale fields receive multiple lines. Accept typing, annotation, dictation, enlarged print, or paper.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Interview Preparation
  • Objective: Students will describe context-appropriate appearance for an interview and prepare truthful, relevant responses and interviewer questions for a mock interview.
  • TEKS: d(6)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Three-page interview-readiness planner plus five-question retryable practice Quiz.

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Post the three-page planner and practice Quiz. Preassign paired, small-group, teacher-conference, private recording, and AAC routes. No student is required to perform publicly or use a camera.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Bellringer - 5 min. Identify what changes across an office interview, a task demonstration, and a virtual interview.
  2. Context model - 8 min. Workplace, task, safety, format, technology, and accommodation come before fashion rules.
  3. Answer model - 8 min. Use situation or task, action, and result or reflection. A school, activity, project, service, or responsibility example is valid; paid work is not required.
  4. Prepare three answers - 14 min. Students build evidence notes rather than memorized scripts.
  5. Interviewer role - 7 min. Prepare a relevant follow-up and a neutral note. Exclude protected or unrelated personal questions.
  6. Practice Quiz - 5 min. Review every feedback explanation.
  7. Exit - 3 min. Record the assigned Day 5 route and one final preparation action.

docs.title: Monitor, Key, and Trim Point
docs.text: Prepared, clean, functional, safe, and role-aware decisions may look different across students and contexts. Eye contact, handshake, expensive or gendered clothing, camera use, and one cultural norm are not universal requirements. An interviewer asks about job evidence, not family, religion, health, disability, immigration, or other protected/private information. Trim optional partner rehearsal before individual preparation.

docs.title: Supports and Access
docs.text: Keep context/contexto, task/tarea, accommodation/adaptación, evidence/evidencia, and follow-up/seguimiento beside the planner. Use the frame: “For a [format/task] interview, Jordan should prepare [action] because [job, safety, technology, or access reason].” Accept short notes, dictation, annotation, enlarged print, paper, AAC, or private conference. Xello Job Interviews is supplemental only.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Mock Interview
  • Objective: Students will describe context-appropriate interview preparation, participate in a mock interview as interviewee and interviewer, revise from feedback, and write appropriate thank-you correspondence.
  • TEKS: d(6)(B), d(6)(C), d(7)(B)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Four-page mock-interview and thank-you record plus the six-criterion Major 1 evidence profile.

docs.title: Before Class
docs.text: Post the four-page record, two-page rubric, and private Major 1 Assignment. Keep Days 1-3 practice evidence available where students already submitted or turned it in; students do not upload the same packet again. Confirm every student's interview route and feedback method before class.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Ready check - 5 min. Open the posting, evidence bank, three answer notes, assigned route, and feedback method.
  2. Round 1 - 10 min. Each student produces assessable interviewee evidence and interviewer evidence through the assigned route.
  3. Feedback and revision - 6 min. Record one specific strength and one exact change.
  4. Round 2 - 10 min. Apply the change in a second response or role exchange.
  5. Thank-you note - 9 min. Draft a brief, specific fictional note. Audit it; do not send it.
  6. Self-score and revision - 7 min. Use all six rubric criteria and revise the weakest available evidence.
  7. Private submit - 3 min. Submit the Day 5 record through the authorized route.

docs.title: Monitor, Key, and Trim Point
docs.text: Interviewee evidence is relevant, truthful, organized, responsive, and visibly revised. Interviewer evidence includes listening, neutral notes, and a job-related follow-up. The thank-you note is brief, specific, accurate, courteous, and unsent. Do not score accent, eye contact, handshake, camera use, clothing cost or style, disability, public confidence, paid work history, or memorization. Trim an extra live exchange, not each student's revision or thank-you evidence.

docs.title: Major 1 Scoring Route
docs.text: Score the Day 1 search/posting record, Day 2 cover letter, Day 3 application and reference protocol, and Day 5 interview/thank-you record with the six-criterion rubric. Earlier Canvas submissions or labeled paper remain the evidence source; students do not compile duplicate uploads. Enter the converted percentage as the score out of 100 in Major Assessments (60%).

docs.title: Supports and Access
docs.text: Keep interviewee/entrevistado, interviewer/entrevistador, follow-up/seguimiento, revision/revisión, and thank-you/agradecimiento beside the record. Use the frame: “I changed [specific response move] after [feedback]. The change helped because [effect].” Partner absence does not block completion. Use a teacher conference, small group, private recording, AAC, or scheduled make-up. Written interviewer notes may show the interviewer role; the interviewee standard still needs assessable spoken or accommodation-aligned communicated evidence.

docs.title: Week 5: Job Search, Applications, and Interviews
docs.text: 6th Six Weeks | 5 class periods | 50 minutes each

docs.title: Weekly Target
docs.text: Students work through one fictional hiring case from posting screen to interview follow-up. They sequence a safe job search, tailor a cover letter, complete a sample application, apply reference protocol, prepare for an interview, participate as interviewer and interviewee, revise from feedback, and write a thank-you note.

docs.title: TEKS Evidence
docs.text:
• d(6)(A): safe seven-step search and posting-screening decision, Day 1.
  • d(7)(B): tailored cover letter and thank-you correspondence, Days 2 and 5.
  • d(7)(C): complete fictional sample application, Day 3.
  • d(7)(D): reference-role selection and permission-before-sharing protocol, Day 3.
  • d(6)(B): workplace, task, safety, format, technology, and access interview-readiness decisions, Days 4-5.
  • d(6)(C): assessable interviewer and interviewee evidence, Day 5.

docs.title: Required Case and Privacy Boundary
docs.text:
The core case is Pecan Creek Animal Care - Student Office Assistant, with fictional applicant Jordan Rivera and an example.com address. The fixed case keeps the work consistent and gives every student the same evidence to reason from.

Students do not enter or submit a real address, phone or email, birth date, student or driver ID, Social Security number, banking or tax data, signature, immigration, health, disability, religion, family information, schedule constraints, or another person's contact information. They do not send an application, permission request, cover letter, or thank-you note and do not contact an employer. FYF Rung 5, Xello Job Interviews, H&L, CareerOneStop tools, and live job boards may extend the lesson after teacher screening; none is required evidence.

docs.title: Week at a Glance
docs.text:
Day Focus Evidence Default Canvas route 1 Search process and posting screen Two-page decision record Private Student Annotation 2 Tailored cover letter Three-page plan, draft, and final Private text, annotation, or upload 3 Application and references Four-page fictional form and protocol Private Student Annotation 4 Interview preparation Three-page rehearsal planner + practice feedback Unlimited-retry practice Quiz 5 Mock interview and follow-up Four-page role, revision, and thank-you record Private Major 1 Assignment

The two-page rubric is posted before Day 2. Earlier practice submissions remain where students completed them; students do not upload the same packet again on Day 5.

docs.title: Teacher Readiness
docs.text:
Post the paired Teacher and Student Guides, named packet or Quiz, and timer. The Teacher Guide contains the fixed case facts, models, answer boundaries, monitoring look-fors, trim point, and absence route. Digital annotation, typed labeled responses, upload, dictation, enlarged print, paper, teacher conference, private recording, and AAC are available when the task calls for them. Pair work supports practice but never determines access to the evidence.

Default printing is zero when students can annotate or type in Canvas. For paper sections, print only the day's packet. Do not print the complete week at once.

docs.title: Assessment Status
docs.text:
The student-visible six-criterion rubric totals 24 raw points and publishes the raw-score-to-percentage conversion. Day 5 is Major 1 in the 6SW assessment map. Canvas records 100 points in Major Assessments (60%); all practice collectors remain 0 points, omitted from the final grade, and unpublished.

Score the six evidence jobs: search/posting screen, cover letter, application, references, mock interview, and thank-you correspondence. Do not score accent, eye contact, handshake, camera use, clothing cost or style, disability, public confidence, paid work history, or English mechanics unless meaning is unclear.

docs.title: Current Teacher Sources
docs.text:
• CareerOneStop Job Search, Cover Letters, Job Applications, References, Interview Preparation, and Follow-Up guidance.
  • EEOC pre-employment guidance for protected, medical, and unrelated personal questions.
  • Xello Job Interviews as an optional licensed extension in authenticated Canvas when available.

docs.title: Access and Absence
docs.text: All required facts and prompts are inside the Canvas pages and packets. A student who misses paired practice uses a teacher conference, small group, private recording, AAC, or scheduled make-up. Written interviewer notes may show the interviewer role; the interviewee standard still requires an assessable spoken or accommodation-aligned communicated response. No family adult, real employer, public Discussion, camera, personal-data disclosure, or external login is required.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Evidence Audit
  • Objective: Students will select a current career pathway or direction using self and career evidence, identify one missing or uncertain evidence job, and document an honest recovery action.
  • TEKS: d(8)(A)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Two-page career-evidence inventory and recovery plan.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Then/now Stop and Jot - 5 min. Name the current direction and one change or stable result.
  2. Model the evidence jobs - 8 min. Show one ready item, one item that needs revision, and one item that needs recovery.
  3. Inventory and active monitoring - 17 min. Students mark eight evidence jobs and name where each item lives or can be rebuilt.
  4. Recovery block - 15 min. Students use one supplied source, prior Canvas artifact, staff conference, or supervised platform catch-up. They write what the evidence supports and what it cannot prove.
  5. Exit - 5 min. Record four pieces to carry forward, one conflict, and the Day 2 priority.

docs.title: Key and Access
docs.text: The recovery action must produce usable current evidence, not a promise to find it later. Do not lower mastery because an old page, family interview, partner, or platform is missing. Preserve the evidence inventory and recovery; trim partner discussion first. No private profile screenshot or contact data.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Career Plan
  • Objective: Students will select a career pathway or direction, document high-school and postsecondary or training requirements, and write an individual plan for starting the career after high school and any postsecondary education.
  • TEKS: d(8)(A), d(8)(B), d(8)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Four-page individual career plan with current evidence, source limits, route questions, three actions, support, and backup.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Model - 5 min. Show how a current plan can be specific without becoming a forever promise.
  2. Current direction - 8 min. Students connect self evidence to a direction, alternative, and career task.
  3. Preparation and labor evidence - 10 min. Students label amount or trend, measure, geography, date, source, and limitation.
  4. High school and training route - 10 min. Students separate a current verified label from a course, application, cost, time, or transportation question that still needs confirmation.
  5. Action plan - 12 min. Students write three actions, dates, an obstacle, a backup, and a support request.
  6. Exit - 5 min. State the strongest evidence and the most important uncertainty.

docs.title: Key and Access
docs.text: Check the evidence basis rather than the student's career preference. A national median is not local starting pay, a pathway label is not an admission guarantee, and a projected trend is not a personal outcome. Students may type, dictate, annotate, use enlarged print, or use paper. Keep the four-page plan in its original Canvas or labeled-paper location for Major 2 scoring; students will not upload it again on Day 4.

docs.title: Day 3: Career Evidence Brief and Rehearsal
Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Presentation Planning
  • Objective: Students will plan and rehearse an oral professional presentation about career and college exploration using appropriate technology, source-labeled evidence, and a privacy-safe route.
  • TEKS: prepares d(4)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Two-page oral/AAC career-evidence brief and rehearsal plan with two timed attempts and one visible revision.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Route and privacy check - 5 min. Confirm live, small-group, conference, private recording, or authorized AAC route and the appropriate technology choice.
  2. Model - 8 min. Show a concise brief with current direction, career task, preparation/labor evidence, high-school/training route, next action, and limitation.
  3. Build the evidence sequence - 17 min. Students use short notes rather than writing a script.
  4. Rehearse twice - 15 min. Time both attempts, collect feedback or use the self-check, and make one visible revision.
  5. Exit - 5 min. Confirm final route, technology, backup, and revision.

docs.title: Key and Access
docs.text: Appropriate technology may be a private Canvas recording, teacher-approved visual or evidence card, or AAC technology. Visual polish, expensive tools, public performance, and camera use are not scored. A written outline supports the brief but does not by itself demonstrate d(4)(C). Preserve the two rehearsals and revision; trim decorative production first.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Professional Presentation
  • Objective: Students will give an oral professional presentation about career and college exploration using appropriate technology, then use feedback to revise one evidence gap.
  • TEKS: d(4)(C), d(8)(B), d(8)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Private 2-3-minute oral/AAC career brief, two-page delivery/revision record, visible revision, transfer action, and six-criterion Major 2 self-score; the Day 2 plan remains in its original location.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Final check - 5 min. Confirm the six speaking jobs, source labels, rubric, route, technology, backup, and privacy boundary.
  2. Parallel delivery block - 22 min. Use small groups, teacher conferences, private recordings, AAC, or a mixed route schedule. Do not run an impossible serial roster.
  3. Feedback - 7 min. Record one effective choice and one exact gap or unclear point.
  4. Revision and transfer - 11 min. Show before/after, explain the improvement, and name one item, question, or dated action to carry forward.
  5. Private submit - 5 min. Submit the Day 4 communicated evidence, two-page record, and self-score once. The teacher scores the Day 2 plan from its original location.

docs.title: Key and Access
docs.text: Score evidence, organization, source labels, audience and time fit, appropriate technology, and visible revision. Do not score accent, eye contact, camera use, public confidence, memorization, disability, or visual polish. A written plan or transcript may scaffold access but does not replace assessable oral/AAC evidence unless an authorized accommodation defines the route.

docs.title: Daily Learning Contract
docs.text:
• Topic: Plan Revision
  • Objective: Students will use specific course evidence to revise an individual plan for starting a career after high school and any postsecondary education, then choose a realistic next action and support.
  • TEKS: d(8)(C)
  • Demonstration of Learning: Two-page private final reflection and transfer plan with then/now evidence, three transferable skills, a dated next action, support, and flexibility note.

docs.title: 50-Minute Flow
docs.text:
1. Then/now Stop and Jot - 5 min. Explain how career planning thinking changed or stayed stable.
  2. Six-weeks evidence map - 12 min. Record one activity, decision, or artifact from each six weeks and what it helped the student understand.
  3. Transferable skills - 10 min. Name three skills, course evidence, and another context for each.
  4. Next action and support - 13 min. Write the action, date, support role, request, realism check, and flexibility response.
  5. Advice and open question - 7 min. Write advice to a future student and one unresolved question.
  6. Private submit - 3 min. Celebration or sharing is optional and consent-based.

docs.title: Key and Access
docs.text: Specific evidence matters more than forced positivity. Students do not need a class photo, public share, family detail, top-career declaration, H&L login, or perfect memory of every week. Provide the module list or six-weeks titles as a recall scaffold. Accept private typed, dictated, annotated, enlarged-print, or paper reflection.

docs.title: Week 6: Career Evidence Capstone
docs.text: 6th Six Weeks | 5 class periods | flexible 50-minute sequence

docs.title: Weekly Target
docs.text: Students recover one missing or uncertain piece of evidence, update a flexible career plan, communicate the plan in a concise oral/AAC career-and-college brief using appropriate technology, revise from feedback, and choose a realistic next action.

docs.title: TEKS Evidence
docs.text:
• d(8)(A): select a current career pathway or direction related to the student's evidence, with a flexible alternative.
  • d(8)(B): document current high-school courses or enrollment actions and postsecondary/training requirements, with unresolved questions labeled.
  • d(8)(C): write an individual plan for starting a career after high school and any postsecondary education.
  • d(4)(C): give an oral professional presentation about career and college exploration using appropriate technology.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The capstone is one evolving evidence record, not five separate portfolios. Day 1 identifies what is ready and recovers one gap. Day 2 creates the four-page career plan. Day 3 prepares the oral/AAC brief. Day 4 communicates and revises the evidence. Day 5 closes the course with a two-page transfer reflection. The Day 2 plan stays where the student first submits or turns it in; Day 4 does not require a duplicate upload.

Missing prior evidence triggers a documented recovery route using a supplied source, teacher/counselor/staff conference, prior Canvas work, or supervised platform catch-up. A missing old workbook page, family interview, H&L login, partner, camera, or public-presentation route does not erase current learning.

docs.title: Week at a Glance
docs.text: Day Focus Durable evidence Canvas interaction 1 Evidence audit and recovery Two-page inventory/recovery plan Private practice Assignment 2 Individual career plan Four-page career plan Private practice Assignment; retained for Major 2 scoring 3 Oral/AAC brief and rehearsal Two-page presentation/rehearsal plan Private practice Assignment 4 Communicated capstone and revision Oral/AAC evidence plus two-page delivery/revision record and rubric Private Major 2 Assignment 5 Reflection and transfer Two-page final reflection and next-action plan Private practice Assignment

docs.title: Grading and Access
docs.text:
The student-visible 24-point evidence profile is Major 2 in the 6SW assessment map. The teacher scores the Day 2 career plan from its original location and the Day 4 communicated evidence, delivery/revision record, and self-score from the mapped Major. Students do not resubmit the Day 2 plan.

Oral/AAC evidence may be live, small group, teacher conference, private audio/video, or an authorized accommodation-aligned route using appropriate technology. A written outline may scaffold the evidence but does not by itself demonstrate d(4)(C). Accent, eye contact, disability, camera use, clothing/style, visual polish, public confidence, and English mechanics are not scored unless meaning is unclear.

docs.title: Licensed and Supplemental Sources
docs.text: FYF Capstone pp. 277-280 and 297-300 are locked Canvas orientation and reflection supports. Students use the custom evidence record because the capstone must remain completable after absence or lost prior work. H&L Career Plan, Xello profile evidence, and earlier course artifacts may supply evidence but are not required completion routes. No new Xello or eDynamic task is assigned in this week.

docs.title: End-of-Year Flexibility
docs.text: If the calendar compresses, preserve Day 1 recovery, the Day 2 career plan, one private Day 4 oral/AAC communication and revision route, and the Day 5 next-action reflection. Combine Days 3-4 or schedule private recordings; cut celebration and decorative production first.

docs.title: Canvas Engagement and Organization Patterns
docs.text:
Status: working production standard for the CCR Canvas course Last checked: August 8, 2026

This guide keeps Canvas from becoming a prettier file cabinet. It also keeps novelty from becoming extra teacher prep. Every tool choice starts with the evidence students need to produce, then uses the lightest interaction that makes that evidence easier to understand, practice, submit, or review.

docs.title: Course organization rule
docs.text:
• One weekly module remains the main path.
  • Every instructional day keeps the same sequence: Day header → Teacher Facilitator Guide → Student Guide → activity.
  • The Student Guide carries the complete purpose, numbered steps, submission route, completion check, absence route, and platform fallback. A quiz, video, discussion, or external tool never becomes the only place where required directions live.
  • Use one primary interaction per day. Add at most one optional enhancement. Students should not have to cross three platforms to prove one idea.
  • Keep practice activities visibly labeled PRACTICE or FORMATIVE. Only the three mapped minors and two mapped majors enter the weighted grade groups.
  • Use module requirements only when order materially protects learning or safety. Do not lock an entire week behind an item that requires manual grading.

This weekly, repeatable structure matches a consistent practitioner finding: teachers report fewer “where is it?” problems when students can stay in Modules, weekly modules follow the same grammar, and graded work appears in a predictable sequence. Practitioner reports also warn that some students navigate from the Dashboard/To Do list instead, so mapped assignments still need clear titles and dates when the calendar is finalized. See the 2024 LMS organization discussion and 2024 Modules/To Do discussion. These are experience reports, not district policy.

docs.title: Interaction selection matrix
docs.text:
Student evidence job Preferred Canvas surface Use when Avoid when Read, orient, or follow a process Native Student Guide page Students need a stable visible route, visuals, disclosures, and absence support Never hide required steps inside collapsed help or a linked file only Write or draw on a structured packet Student Annotation Assignment The packet already has correctly sized response space and students benefit from writing directly on it Do not use if the PDF fields are cramped, split across pages badly, or inaccessible without a paper/typed route Submit extended reasoning, a file, or media Private Assignment with multiple submission types The evidence can be typed, uploaded, recorded, annotated, dictated, or completed on paper Do not require a public post or a single software format Practice a bounded decision with immediate feedback Ungraded, retryable Quiz Each option can receive a useful explanation and the item has a defensible key Do not turn every reflection into multiple choice or use a quiz for evidence that needs explanation/design Analyze an image, diagram, or message Embedded visual + annotation or short response Students need to mark clues, compare regions, or explain visible evidence Do not use unreadable full-page screenshots or color alone Watch a short model or demonstration Captioned Canvas Studio embed A 1–5 minute clip reduces teacher explanation and has a transcript/captions Do not use a long passive video, autoplay, or video as the only absence route Learn from peers Small-group Discussion or structured reply Comparing genuinely different solutions improves the work and privacy risk is low Do not post career profiles, financial priorities, personal results, health details, or a public performance requirement Build a shared map or sort Lucid Whiteboard LTI or teacher-provided board A group must organize multiple relationships and each student has an equal non-dragging role Do not use when a simple table is clearer or when the board creates login/access friction Create a designed product Canva for Education LTI, Adobe Express, or paper Visual communication is part of the evidence and a plain/paper route earns the same score Do not grade software polish, require public publishing, or make a copied template the evidence Capture oral/AAC evidence Private media Assignment, Studio, or teacher conference Oral communication is actually being assessed and students have equivalent routes Do not substitute written notes for oral evidence unless an accommodation changes the task Differentiate after evidence Teacher-assigned support/recovery item; later Mastery Paths pilot The source item is already stable, grading turnaround is fast, and the SIS effect has been tested Do not deploy coursewide before the core path is finished

Canvas supports weighted Assignment Groups, module requirements, prerequisites, and conditional Mastery Paths. Official guidance warns that manually graded source work can delay Mastery Path access and differentiated items may not sync automatically to every SIS. For this course, Mastery Paths are a later pilot—not a foundation dependency. See Canvas module settings and Canvas Mastery Paths.

docs.title: 1. Model → try → feedback
docs.text: Use a short captioned model, then one retryable check, then the authentic artifact. This is a good fit for phishing decisions, source labels, code specificity, interview boundaries, and safety choices. The quiz is practice; the artifact carries the reasoning.

docs.title: 2. Embedded licensed video with a native route
docs.text:
Where Xello supplies a student video, facilitator guide, worksheet, or slide deck:

  1. store the licensed file only in locked Canvas;
  2. embed the video at the exact step where it is used;
  3. provide captions or a transcript;
  4. state the required Xello completion separately;
  5. keep a native text/screenshot route for absence and review;
  6. record the source, access date, and licensing boundary in the teacher guide.

Canvas Studio is installed in the live CCR course. Studio can support captioned embedded media and interactive video questions, but video-quiz gradebook behavior must be tested in this district course before it becomes graded evidence. Use embedded checks first as comprehension pauses.

docs.title: 3. Student annotation instead of printing
docs.text:
If a worksheet asks students to label, circle, sketch, or complete a short table, attach the verified PDF to a Student Annotation Assignment. Before import, inspect every page at realistic print and Chromebook size:

  • one-line fact = one line;
  • explanation = at least 3–5 full-width lines;
  • paragraph = 6–9 lines or a typed field;
  • sketch = at least half a portrait page or a clearly labeled landscape panel;
  • comparison table = no long prose in narrow cells;
  • bilingual labels do not reduce the response area.

The paper, typed, dictated, enlarged-print, and annotation routes use the same success criteria.

docs.title: 4. Private first, social only when social matters
docs.text: Use Discussions for peer interpretation, critique, or multiple defensible solutions—not because a worksheet has a final question. Give roles or a response frame, require one evidence-based contribution, and offer a private equivalent when public participation is not part of the standard.

docs.title: 5. Teacher dashboard at the top of each guide
docs.text:
The first screen of every Teacher Guide should answer:

  • What do I open before class?
  • What must students finish?
  • What is the 50-minute flow and trim point?
  • What answer/model do I need?
  • What do I check in Canvas or Xello afterward?
  • What happens if the platform, equipment, partner, or prior artifact is missing?

Optional extensions, research links, and alternate tools belong below this core dashboard.

docs.title: Live integration inventory
docs.text:
The course navigation observed on August 8, 2026 includes Canvas Studio, Canva for Education, Lucid Whiteboard, Office 365, Collaborations, BigBlueButton, Zoom, Discovery Education, and other district LTIs. Presence in navigation proves availability to the instructor account; it does not by itself prove student provisioning, privacy approval for a specific task, grade passback, mobile behavior, or accessibility.

Before an integration becomes required:

  1. launch it from the student view or a test student;
  2. confirm no account creation or personal-data collection is added;
  3. verify Chromebook/mobile behavior;
  4. verify captions, keyboard access, contrast, and screen-reader labels;
  5. verify whether work returns to Canvas and what the teacher sees;
  6. run the absence/platform fallback;
  7. measure teacher setup and grading time;
  8. keep it unpublished until those checks pass.

docs.title: Variety without chaos
docs.text:
Across a five-day week, aim for different cognitive actions, not five different apps. A balanced pattern might be:

  • Day 1: visual source analysis;
  • Day 2: retryable decision practice;
  • Day 3: individual design or structured annotation;
  • Day 4: small-group test/compare with individual evidence;
  • Day 5: private synthesis, media brief, or portfolio revision.

The same Canvas grammar stays stable while the thinking changes. That is the balance: predictable navigation, varied work.

docs.title: August 8, 2026 follow-up research pass
docs.text:
A current official/practitioner scan reinforced the existing Modules-first design and added four publication checks:

  1. Keep one source of truth. Current middle-school Canvas users repeatedly describe weekly modules, day subheaders, and directly adjacent activities as easier for students and absent learners. They also warn that repeating directions in Pages, Assignments, Files, and a separate syllabus creates update drift. The Student Guide remains the complete route; an Assignment or external tool links back to it instead of copying a second version of the directions. See the 2025 middle-school organization discussion and 2026 teacher-planner discussion. These posts are implementation signals, not evidence or policy.
  2. Audit student navigation before publication. Instructure documents that instructors can hide or disable course-navigation links while still seeing them as teachers. After the core route passes Student View, evaluate whether Pages, Files, Quizzes, and unused LTIs should be hidden so students do not bypass the weekly sequence. Do not change navigation merely to make the teacher view look cleaner. See Instructure: manage Course Navigation links.
  3. Use requirements as progress signals, not punishment. A Mark as Done page requirement can create a visible completion check, while a submission requirement can confirm that an activity was turned in. Requirements and prerequisites can also re-lock or delay students after edits. Pilot them on one stable week, never behind manual grading, and confirm the absent/late-work route before coursewide use. See Instructure: edit module requirements and prerequisites.
  4. Pilot anonymous peer review only where critique matters. Canvas can assign anonymous peer reviews and attach a rubric, which can reduce social pressure and teacher matching work. Canvas DocViewer annotations do not remain anonymous, and late or missing submissions can strand reviewers. Use this only for a stable draft-review lesson with a private teacher/self-review fallback; do not attach it to personal career profiles or sensitive reflection. See the Canvas Basics Guide, updated June 27, 2025.

No new integration became load-bearing from this scan. Studio, Canva, Lucid, annotation, peer review, and requirements remain targeted pilots that must pass student provisioning, accessibility, privacy, mobile, fallback, and teacher-time checks in the live Irving course.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• The interaction improves a defined evidence job.
  • Required directions remain visible in the Student Guide.
  • Teacher setup takes no more than the guide states.
  • The worksheet or digital field has enough response space.
  • The tool has an equal absence/platform route.
  • Licensed content remains in locked Canvas.
  • No personal profile, family financial, health, contact, or application data is exposed.
  • Captions/transcript, alt text, keyboard route, contrast, and non-color cues are present.
  • The activity is correctly labeled practice, formative, minor, major, or recovery.
  • Student view and teacher view both pass before publishing.

docs.title: Facilitation Strategies
docs.text: Use these discussion and reading structures when a daily plan calls for students to read together or discuss as a class, but the default routine is not working. The daily plan supplies the content and time; this page gives the teacher a way to organize the talk or reading without changing the activity.

docs.title: How to Pick a Strategy
docs.text:
• By activity type. Partner talk: Think-Pair-Share, RallyRobin. Dense reading: Talk-Read-Talk-Write, Jigsaw. Accountable check: QSSA. Seat-mixer: Stand Up Hand Up Pair Up.
  • By time budget. Under 5 min: RallyRobin or QSSA. 5 to 10 min: Think-Pair-Share, RoundRobin. 15+ min: Talk-Read-Talk-Write, Jigsaw.
  • By rigor target. DOK 1 recall: RallyRobin, Think-Pair-Share. DOK 2 analysis: Talk-Read-Talk-Write, Jigsaw. DOK 3 application: QSSA with a scenario stem.

docs.title: QSSA (Question, Signal, Stem, Answer)
docs.text:
Time: 3 to 5 min | Group size: whole class | Best for: accountable talk, quick formative check, a DOK 2 question mid-activity

  1. Question. Ask a question aligned to the lesson objective.
  2. Signal. Students signal when they have an answer (thumb at chest, pencil down, hand up).
  3. Stem. Provide a sentence stem ("One reason is _ because ___").
  4. Answer. Students share with a partner using the stem. Cold-call 1 to 2 students to repeat their partner's answer using the stem.

CCE fit: warm-ups where every student needs time to think, exit-ticket pre-checks, and DOK 2 questions inside a daily plan.

docs.title: Think-Pair-Share
docs.text:
Time: 4 to 6 min | Group size: partners | Best for: warm-ups, low-risk participation, vocabulary introduction

  1. Think (60 sec). Students silently think and jot a bullet or one word.
  2. Pair (90 to 120 sec). Partners share. Each partner must contribute before anyone talks twice.
  3. Share (1 to 2 min). Cold-call or take volunteers. Students may share their partner's idea, not only their own.

CCE fit: most warm-ups, introducing H&L vocabulary (Climber, Hat, cluster), DOK 2 questions mid-activity.

docs.title: Talk-Read-Talk-Write
docs.text:
Time: 15 to 25 min | Group size: partners or quads | Best for: dense reading passages where students tend to skim, H&L chapter openers, pathway readouts

  1. Talk (3 to 5 min). Partners predict what a passage will say based on the title, headings, or a preview image.
  2. Read (8 to 15 min). Students read silently or in pairs (alternating paragraphs).
  3. Talk (3 to 5 min). Partners discuss: what matched our prediction? What surprised us?
  4. Write (3 to 5 min). Students write individually (exit ticket, stop-and-jot, journal reflection).

CCE fit: H&L chapter openers, the six-pathway readouts (e.g., Ch 14 p. 230), Powerskills modules that students otherwise skim.

docs.title: Jigsaw
docs.text:
Time: 15 to 20 min | Group size: expert groups of 4 to 6, then mixed home groups | Best for: parallel content where each sub-section has the same structure (6 pathways, 14 clusters, 6 personality types)

  1. Assign (1 min). Divide students into expert groups. Assign each group ONE sub-section (one Manufacturing pathway, one core personality type, one cluster).
  2. Expert (6 to 8 min). Groups read and discuss their sub-section. Each member writes 2 to 3 key points in their workbook.
  3. Remix (1 min). Re-sort students so every new home group has one expert from each original group.
  4. Teach (6 to 8 min). Experts teach their sub-section to the home group. Peers take notes.

CCE fit: 1SW Wk1 Day 1 (6 Manufacturing pathways), any week teaching parallel H&L chapter lists.

Differentiation note: Pair ELL students with a bilingual peer in the expert group so they can process in L1 before teaching in L2. For students with reading-level gaps, assign them the sub-section with the most visual support in the workbook.

docs.title: Kagan: RallyRobin
docs.text:
Time: 2 to 3 min | Group size: partners | Best for: a quick brainstorm in which both partners answer

  1. Pose a question with many possible answers ("Name a career in Manufacturing", "Name a daily object that was manufactured").
  2. Partners alternate answers, one at a time, back and forth, until time is called.
  3. Cold-call 2 to 3 pairs to share the best answer they heard.

CCE fit: warm-ups asking for examples, rapid recall of career clusters, Work Values brainstorm.

docs.title: Kagan: RoundRobin
docs.text:
Time: 4 to 6 min | Group size: quads | Best for: a discussion in which each student gets a turn

  1. Pose a question.
  2. Students in each table group of 4 share one answer in order, clockwise. No interruptions.
  3. After one full round, the group picks the best answer and one student reports out.

CCE fit: Work Values discussion, cluster favorites, reflection on a Hat that students researched.

docs.title: Kagan: Stand Up Hand Up Pair Up
docs.text:
Time: 3 to 5 min | Group size: whole class, random partners | Best for: mixer, finding a partner outside the usual seat group

  1. Students stand, hand up, and walk the room. The first classmate they meet with hand up becomes their partner.
  2. Partners discuss the teacher's question (pair with Think-Pair-Share or QSSA).
  3. Call time. Students return to their seats.

CCE fit: Week 0 classroom community building, mid-year cluster check-ins, any week where the seat-partner pattern has gone stale.

docs.title: Six-Weeks Grading Framework
docs.text:
The coursewide placement of the three Minor and two Major assessments in each block is maintained in the Six-Weeks Assessment Map. Weekly products not listed there remain formative or recovery evidence even when they have a complete rubric.

Use this framework when setting up the CCE gradebook. The module-level assessment map will identify the exact assignments used in each six-weeks block.

docs.title: Required grade mix
docs.text:
Category Six-weeks weight Minimum entries Minor grades 40% 3 Major grades 60% 2

Do not count every daily exit ticket as a separate grade. Exit tickets are primarily formative evidence the teacher uses to decide whether to reteach, extend, or regroup. A teacher may combine a purposeful set of exit tickets into one minor checkpoint when the set measures a coherent skill.

docs.title: Minor grades
docs.text:
Use minor grades for completed checkpoints that show progress toward the week's or block's larger product. Suitable evidence includes:

  • a completed research or comparison worksheet
  • a platform completion standard with a reflection or saved profile artifact
  • a design checkpoint or revision
  • a short written explanation tied to the learning target
  • a selected set of exit tickets measuring the same skill

Completion alone is not enough when the task is supposed to show reasoning. Use the linked checklist, answer key, or rubric.

docs.title: Major grades
docs.text:
Use major grades for products that require students to apply several parts of the block. Suitable evidence includes:

  • the six-weeks summative portfolio or project
  • a performance task scored with a rubric
  • the block CFA after its teacher-feedback gate is complete
  • a career plan, presentation, mock interview, or other TEKS-aligned capstone product

Every major grade needs a student-visible scoring tool before students begin the final product.

docs.title: Performance bands
docs.text:
Score Performance band 90-100 Masters 80-89 Meets 70-79 Approaches 60-69 Needs Improvement

Scores below 60 follow campus or district grading policy. This curriculum does not assign an additional label or invent a recovery rule.

docs.title: Teacher setup check
docs.text:
Before the six weeks begins, confirm:

  1. At least three minor and two major assignments are identified.
  2. The category and point value are visible to students.
  3. Every graded product has a linked rubric, checklist, or answer key.
  4. Xello, H&L, and other platform evidence is described as an artifact the teacher can verify.
  5. Absent students have a completion route that measures the same learning.
  6. The final grade mix calculates to 40% minor and 60% major.

The approved block-by-block placements are maintained in the Six-Weeks Assessment Map. Do not substitute a polished weekly product for one of those entries without an intentional assessment-map revision; the map protects the 3-Minor/2-Major limit and prevents practice work from silently becoming extra grades.

docs.title: Health Science Extension Topics
docs.text:
The curriculum does not dedicate a week to these three health science specialties, although students may ask about them and related careers appear in Irving ISD pathways. The sections below record where each specialty could connect to an existing lesson. They are planning notes until the health science coordinator team supplies sources.

Status: Awaiting source materials from Irving ISD health science coordinators. Do not promote these sections into primary weekly content until the SOURCE_PENDING tags below are removed and citations are added.

docs.title: Physical Therapy (PT) and Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA)
docs.text:
Integration hooks in existing curriculum:

  • 2SW Wk3 (Nursing / Health Science) Day 1 career research: students with Helper and Doer core personality types can add PT to the careers they compare.
  • 2SW Wk6 (Biomedical / Health Science) Days 2-4: the Mark athlete-rehabilitation scenario gives coordinators a place to add PT if they later approve a sourced activity.
  • 6SW Wk1 (Education / Community) Day 4: PT volunteer/shadow hours at a PT clinic fit as a community service option.

What to fill in once source is available:

  • DFW entry-level salary for PTA (currently BLS national median is the fallback)
  • Irving ISD pathway connection (if any; currently Medical Therapeutics at Singley touches this lightly)
  • Specific H&L Hat profile match and workbook chapter citation
  • Education pathway: Associate (PTA) vs Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) distinction

docs.title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography
docs.text:
Integration hooks in existing curriculum:

  • 2SW Wk3 (Nursing / Health Science) Day 3 micro:bit vital signs activity: add sonography to the career comparison when the lesson moves from vital signs to diagnostic equipment.
  • 2SW Wk4 (Dental / Medical Billing) Day 4 health informatics career research: sonography fits the high-skill-high-demand classification.
  • 5SW Wk2 (Civil Engineering) Day 4: imaging technology has civil engineering cross-links (bridge ultrasonic inspection).

What to fill in once source is available:

  • DFW DMS training programs (community college partnerships)
  • ARDMS certification pathway (what's required, how long, how expensive)
  • Specific H&L Hat profile match and workbook chapter citation
  • Irving ISD pathway connection (Medical Therapeutics Singley likely overlaps)

docs.title: Sports Medicine and Athletic Training
docs.text:
Integration hooks in existing curriculum:

  • 2SW Wk3 (Nursing / Health Science) Day 1 career research worksheet: students with Doer, Helper, and Achievement results can add Athletic Trainer to the careers they compare.
  • 2SW Wk3 (Nursing / Health Science) Days 3-4 Vitals in Motion: the community fun-run medical tent is the existing lesson context for sourced sports-medicine material. The old athlete-rehabilitation day is no longer in the curriculum.
  • 3SW Wk5 (Cosmetology) Day 4 Stress Toolkit: sports med connects to the wellness-adjacent careers branch.
  • 6SW Wk4 (Sales / Presentations) Day 3: sports agency and sports PR overlap with sports medicine careers.

What to fill in once source is available:

  • Difference between Athletic Trainer (AT), Sports Physical Therapist (SPT), and Sports Medicine Physician
  • NATA BOC certification for ATs
  • Irving ISD pathway connection (possibly Health Science or Medical Therapeutics)
  • Specific H&L Hat profile match and workbook chapter citation
  • Clinical vs. scholastic sports med context (high school AT vs. pro team AT)

docs.title: How to Drop in Source Content
docs.text:
When a coordinator delivers source material for any of the three sections above:

  1. Remove the corresponding <!-- SOURCE_PENDING: ... --> tag.
  2. Replace the "What to fill in" checklist with concrete content (named H&L chapter, citable BLS data, specific Irving ISD pathway, etc.).
  3. Add the section to the appropriate week's Overview "Irving ISD Pathway" note if there's a direct pathway match.
  4. Consider whether the source content is substantial enough to promote from this resource page into a day-file Extension section. If yes, move it and leave a pointer here.

Grep recipe for finding all pending source placeholders:

grep -rn "SOURCE_PENDING" docs/

docs.title: Resources Status & Backlog
docs.text:
What this page is: a living checklist of teacher-facing resources that are ready to use, partially built, or still to be created for the CCE Curriculum. This is the page to check when you want to know "what's missing before I can teach this week" or "what should I expect my teammates to build next."

docs.title: Exit-ticket PDF pipeline
docs.text:
Every daily exit ticket renders to a printable, Irving ISD branded PDF. 178 PDFs cover all 180 daily plans except 1SW Wk3 Day 3 and 1SW Wk5 Day 5, which have no exit ticket. Each day page carries a [Printable PDF] link next to its **EXIT TICKET** marker.

python3 build/build_pdfs.py         # regenerate every exit-ticket PDF
python3 build/inject_pdf_links.py   # refresh the [Printable PDF] links in day files

Operating manual: cce-curriculum/notes/exit-ticket-pdf-pipeline.md. Do not hand-edit the generated PDFs or the design CSS in build/exit_ticket_template/.

Classroom printables (worksheets, rubrics, contracts, references, and scaffolds) have their own generator. docs.title: New hard dependencies from the Phase B realignment (2026-08-05)
docs.text:
Realigning 2SW and 3SW to Find Your Future introduced three supply requirements that did not exist before. These are not "nice to have" enrichment; the named days do not run without them.

Week What it needs Why 2SW Wk2 Days 2-4 (Law Enforcement / EMT) The Clinton Lake Case Climber Notes deck (six evidence files, slides 2-7) and the Injured on the Trail Climber Notes deck (supply table plus the sling and finger-splint technique photos, slides 2-3) Both decks are teacher-side only. The evidence files and the technique photos are not printed in the student workbook, so Days 2 through 4 have no content without them. Decks are on hand at cce-curriculum/resources/climber-notes/ 2SW Wk2 Days 3-4 (Law Enforcement / EMT) Per-pair first-aid supplies: one triangular bandage or equivalent cloth for the sling, tape, and a popsicle stick or similar rigid splint for the finger Students take turns as responder and injured hiker and physically apply a sling and a splint. Budget one set per pair, not one per class 3SW Wk5 Days 1-3 (Cosmetology) Special effects makeup supplies: tissue or cotton for texture, liquid latex or a school-safe adhesive alternative, cream or water-based color, tweezers, and a skin-safe base surface Special Effects Makeup is the only FYF activity the workbook itself splits across three days, and Day 2 is a hands-on build. Check student allergies before ordering; the latex substitute is the usual accommodation

Two Climber Notes decks are also load-bearing in Health Science: Vitals in Motion (2SW Wk3, the tool reference and the fever, blood pressure, and pulse oximeter charts) and Smile Squad (2SW Wk4, Mia's five X-rays). Their selected instructional visuals are embedded in the locked, unpublished Canvas modules with teacher guidance and accessible student routes. The source .pptx binaries remain gitignored and are not exposed on this public site.

docs.text:
Realigning 4SW, 5SW, and 6SW added four more deck dependencies and one scheduling load. Without the projected images there is nothing for students to inspect, and the written inspection report on Day 5 has no source 5SW Wk4 Day 2 (HVAC / Electrical / Plumbing) The PowerSkill Written Communication deck (four service ticket photos, slides 2-5) Students write four technician field notes from the photos. The workbook prints the format and the worked example but not the tickets 5SW Wk4 Day 5 (HVAC / Electrical / Plumbing) The Plumbing Under Pressure deck (slide 2) plus chart paper or poster board and markers, one set per team of 3 Teams sketch and label the work zone before presenting the emergency plan 4SW Wk3 Day 2 (Aviation) The Flight Line Fixers deck (aircraft inspection photos, slides 2-6) This is the only aviation activity in the workbook and it runs as an extension.
